source_text: Si filii, et heredes: heredes quidem Dei, coheredes autem Christi. Expectatio creaturae revelationem filiorum Dei expectat. Gloria Spiritui. Amen.
thought_title: Heirs with Christ and creation's expectation
orientation: Origen is quoting and glossing Paul's words from Romans 8 about believers as God's children and heirs, and creation awaiting the revelation of God's children.
pass_a_gloss: If [we are] children, also [we are] heirs: heirs indeed of God, coheirs moreover of Christ. [The] expectation [of] the creation [the] revelation [of the] children of God awaits. Glory [to the] Spirit. Amen.

choices.why: Keeps the conditional force and the compact Pauline phrasing; 'et' here means 'also' in the apodosis.
'Autem' marks a contrastive addition, so 'moreover' preserves the adversative-connective force; 'co-heirs' keeps the compound noun parallel to 'heirs.'

choices.term: Expectatio creaturae revelationem filiorum Dei expectat
choices.english: The expectation of creation awaits the revelation of the children of God
choices.why: The cognate accusative construction (expectatio...expectat) is kept literally to show the rhetorical repetition; 'awaits' preserves the present tense and forward-looking sense.
rejected: Creation waits with eager longing for the revealing of the sons of God
The eager expectation of the creation waits for the revelation of God's sons

choices.why: A doxological formula; the dative 'Spiritui' is rendered with 'to' to show it is the recipient of glory, and 'the Spirit' follows the glossary for Spiritus.

bible_refs.note: Si filii, et heredes: heredes quidem Dei, coheredes autem Christi
Expectatio creaturae revelationem filiorum Dei expectat

pass_b_english: If children, also heirs: heirs indeed of God, co-heirs moreover of Christ (Romans 8:17). The expectation of creation awaits the revelation of the children of God (Romans 8:19). Glory to the Spirit. Amen.

last_rejected.why: Latin dative 'Spiritui' is ambiguous: could mean 'to the Spirit' or 'of the Spirit'. Context suggests 'Glory of the Spirit' or 'Glory be to the Spirit' as doxology. 'Glory to the Spirit' is possible but less certain; the phrase is abrupt and may represent a marginal gloss or liturgical insertion, not Origen's commentary voice.
last_rejected.ruling: Dative 'Spiritui' naturally renders 'to the Spirit'; 'Gloria Spiritui' is a standard doxology. Translator's choice is within normal range.
